bib.title: Beyond I.I.D.: Three Levels of Generalization for Question Answering on Knowledge Bases

question: How well do KBQA models generalize beyond i.i.d. to compositional and zero-shot questions on a large knowledge base, and what helps?
hypothesis: Pre-trained contextual embeddings such as BERT and question-specific search space pruning are key to compositional and zero-shot generalization.
contributions: First systematic study of three levels of generalization (i.i.d., compositional, zero-shot) for KBQA
GrailQA: 64K-question crowdsourced Freebase dataset supporting all three levels
BERT-based Seq2Seq KBQA model (Transduction and Ranking) with analyses showing the role of BERT in generalization

method.summary: Builds GrailQA by generating Freebase logical forms (Su et al. 2016 algorithm), validating them, annotating canonical questions and crowd-paraphrasing them, then sampling groundings. Proposes a BERT-encoded LSTM Seq2Seq model that outputs S-expressions, run either as generator (Transduction) or as a ranker over enumerated 2-hop candidates (Ranking), and evaluates on split i.i.d./compositional/zero-shot test sets.
method.task: KBQA / semantic parsing of questions to S-expression logical forms over Freebase

datasets.name: GrailQA
datasets.split: train/val/test 44,337 / 6,763 / 13,231 (about 70/10/20); val and test: 50% zero-shot, 25% compositional, 25% i.i.d.; 5 held-out domains for validation and 10 for test
datasets.source: Freebase Commons (86 domains, 2,038 classes, 6,265 relations, over 45M entities); CC-BY 4.0 paper
datasets.preprocessing: logical forms up to 4 relations plus at most one function (count, argmax/argmin, comparatives); sampling weights divided by rho_l=2 (logical form) and rho_p=10 (paraphrase); entity surface forms mined from FACC1

datasets.name: WebQ (WebQuestions)
datasets.source: Berant et al. 2013; Yih et al. 2016 logical forms

models.name: Transduction (BERT)
models.architecture: LSTM encoder-decoder Seq2Seq, tied input/output embeddings from BERT; dynamic vocabulary pruned to items within 2 hops of linked entities
models.vocab: dynamic per question (schema items, entities, functions, syntax constants)
models.context: 512 tokens BERT limit; vocabulary split into chunks concatenated with question

models.name: Ranking (BERT)
models.architecture: Same Seq2Seq used to score candidate logical forms enumerated within 2 hops of linked entities

models.name: GloVe variants (-BERT)
models.architecture: Same models with average GloVe-6B-300d embedding per schema item, GloVe fixed

models.name: QGG (Lan and Jiang 2020)
models.architecture: Query graph generation, RL, BERT as one of 7 hand-crafted ranking features; 2-hop candidates

models.name: BERT NER entity linker
models.architecture: BERT-based NER trained on GrailQA training set, disambiguation by FACC1 popularity

training.objective: Seq2Seq log-likelihood p(a|q)=prod p(y_t|y_<t,q) (Eq 1); for Ranking used to score candidates
training.lr: 0.001 for own parameters; 2e-5 for BERT parameters
training.batch_size: 32 for GloVe models; 1 for BERT models with gradient accumulation 16
training.epochs: early stopping, patience 3, best validation exact match

other.fine_tune_BERT: yes; GloVe fixed because fine-tuning it was slightly worse
other.vocabulary_pruning: applied in training and inference for BERT models, not needed in GloVe training

inference.decoding: Transduction: autoregressive until stop token (search method, beam size not stated); Ranking: score all enumerated candidates, return top
inference.retrieval: Candidate enumeration: all logical forms (optional COUNT) within 2 hops of identified entities; recall 80%; vocabulary pruning to 2 hops of anchor entities

parameters.BERT_chunk: vocabulary items split into chunks, each concatenated with the question

metrics.name: Exact match (EM)
metrics.definition: Percent of questions whose predicted and gold logical forms are semantically equivalent, via graph isomorphism after converting S-expressions to graph queries

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: F1 between predicted and gold answer sets, answers computed from a local Virtuoso SPARQL endpoint

eval.protocol: Single run on validation/test; robustness analysis assumes perfect entity linking with upper/lower bounds by paraphrase and template grouping; error analysis on 100 random Ranking errors

limits: Ranking candidates cover only about 80% of questions; enumerates only up to 2 relations because 3 hops is prohibitively many
Ranking and QGG fail on superlatives/comparatives, which usually lack a topic entity
Entity linking is a major bottleneck (33% of errors)
Authors say there is a lack of deeper understanding of why BERT helps
Freebase has stopped being updated; models are LSTM+BERT-base, pre-LLM; no LLM/prompting baselines
Single runs, no seeds or variance reported

terms.definition: Every test question's schema items appear in training but its specific logical form is not covered in training
Test question contains at least one schema item (relation, class, function) not in training
Test schema items all in training and test questions follow the training distribution
Linearised logical form with set-based semantics using AND, COUNT, R, JOIN, ARGMAX, ARGMIN, LT, LE, GT, GE
Keep only KB items reachable within 2 hops of entities identified in the question
